course.title: JavaScript Programming
course.tagline: Master JavaScript from the basics to real projects: apps, games and interactive pages.

days.title: What JavaScript Is and Your First Script
days.goal: Understand what JavaScript does in a web page and run your first line of it.

video.title: JavaScript Full Course for Beginners | Complete All-in-One Tutorial | 8 Hours

steps: Make a folder called js-journey and create index.html with a basic page.
Add a <script> tag at the end of the body and write console.log('Hello, world!').
Open the page in Chrome, press F12 and read your message in the Console tab.
Change the message, refresh the page and see it update.
days.task: Build a page that prints your name, your age and one goal in the console.
days.challenge: Use alert() to show a pop-up message, then change it to console.log() and compare.

quiz.q: What does JavaScript do in a web page?
options: It makes the page interactive: it reacts, changes things and talks to servers
It stores the page on a server
quiz.explain: JavaScript adds behaviour: clicks, changes, calculations and data fetching.

quiz.q: Where do you see console.log() output?
options: In the browser developer tools Console tab
quiz.explain: console.log() prints to the browser console, which you open with F12.

options: It tells the browser to run JavaScript code
quiz.explain: Code inside a <script> tag runs when the page loads.

days.title: Variables: let, const and var
days.goal: Store values with let and const and know when to use each one.

video.title: Full JavaScript Course for Beginners

steps: Declare a name with let and change it, then print both values.
Declare a birthYear with const and try to change it to see the error.
Make a variable for your age and one for your city, then log a sentence using both.
Try var once and notice it behaves like let for simple cases.
days.task: Write a script with variables for a product name, price and stock count, then log a neat summary.
days.challenge: Swap two variables using a third temporary variable and log the result.

quiz.q: What is the difference between let and const?
options: let can be reassigned, const cannot
const can be reassigned, let cannot
quiz.explain: let lets you change the value later. const locks it after the first assignment.

quiz.q: What happens if you try to change a const?
quiz.explain: Reassigning a const throws a TypeError. That is the point of const.

quiz.q: Which should you use by default?
options: const, and let only when the value must change
quiz.explain: Use const by default. It protects you from accidental changes. Use let only when the value must change.

days.title: Data Types and Operators
days.goal: Know the main data types and use maths and comparison operators.

video.title: JavaScript Tutorial for Beginners - Full Course in 12 Hours (2022)

steps: Log the type of a string, a number, a boolean, undefined and null using typeof.
Try + - * / and % with two numbers and log each answer.
Compare 5 == '5' and 5 === '5' and notice the difference.
Use > < >= <= to compare two ages and log true or false.
days.task: Write a script that checks if a person is old enough to vote and logs the answer.
days.challenge: Work out the price of 3 items with a 10% discount using only JavaScript maths.

quiz.explain: === is strict equality. It checks both the value and the type.

quiz.q: What is the type of null?
quiz.explain: typeof null returns 'object'. This is a famous old quirk in JavaScript.
% gives the remainder. 10 divided by 3 leaves 1.

days.title: Strings
days.goal: Work with text: join strings, use template literals and change case.

video.title: JavaScript Full Course For Beginners With JavaScript Projects

steps: Join a first name and last name with + and log the full name.
Use a template literal with backticks and ${name} to build a greeting.
Use .length to count the letters in a word.
Use .toUpperCase() and .toLowerCase() on a sentence.
days.task: Build a program that asks for a name with prompt() and greets the user by name in capital letters.
days.challenge: Take a sentence and log its first letter, its last letter and its length.

options: A string in backticks that lets you put ${variables} inside
A string that is always empty
quiz.explain: Template literals use backticks and ${} to drop values straight into text.
length counts the characters. 'hello' has 5.
toUpperCase() returns a new string with all letters capitalised.

days.title: Numbers and Maths
days.goal: Do maths in JavaScript and handle numbers that come in as text.

video.title: JavaScript Tutorial For Beginners

steps: Use Math.round(), Math.floor() and Math.ceil() on 4.7 and log the results.
Use Math.random() to get a random number between 0 and 1.
Use Number('42') to turn text into a number and add 8 to it.
Use .toFixed(2) to show a price with two decimal places.
days.task: Build a tip calculator: ask for a bill amount and a tip percent, then log the tip and the total.
days.challenge: Generate a random whole number from 1 to 100 and log it.

quiz.explain: floor() rounds down to the nearest whole number, so 4.9 becomes 4.
Number('7') turns the text into the number 7, so 7 + 3 is 10.

options: A decimal from 0 up to (but not including) 1
quiz.explain: Math.random() gives a decimal from 0 to just under 1. Multiply and floor it to get a range.

days.title: If, Else and Comparisons
days.goal: Make decisions with if, else if and else.

video.title: JavaScript Full Course for Beginners (2026): Build a Real Page

steps: Write an if that logs 'Adult' when age is 18 or more.
Add an else if for ages 13 to 17 that logs 'Teenager', and an else that logs 'Child'.
Use && to check two things at once, like age >= 18 && hasID.
Use || to check if either of two things is true.
days.task: Build a program that asks for a score and logs A, B, C or F.
days.challenge: Ask for a password with prompt() and log 'Welcome' only if it matches.

quiz.q: What does && mean in a condition?
quiz.explain: && means AND. Both sides must be true for the whole condition to be true.

quiz.q: When does the else block run?
options: Only when the if and else if checks are all false
quiz.explain: else runs only when every check above it was false.

options: OR: at least one side must be true
quiz.explain: || means OR. The condition is true when at least one side is true.

days.title: Project 1: Guessing Game in the Browser
days.goal: Build a number guessing game that runs on a web page.

video.title: Code Companion #9: DOM Manipulation

steps: Make an HTML page with an input box, a button and a message area.
Pick a secret number with Math.floor(Math.random() * 20) + 1.
When the button is clicked, read the guess and say 'too high' or 'too low'.
Count the tries and show a win message when the guess is right.
days.task: Finish the guessing game and play it until you win.
days.challenge: Add a limit of 5 guesses. If the player runs out, reveal the secret number.

quiz.q: How do you read what a user typed in an input?
quiz.explain: You select the input element and read its .value property.

options: A random whole number from 1 to 20
quiz.explain: random() * 20 gives 0 to just under 20, floor makes it 0-19, and + 1 shifts it to 1-20.

quiz.q: Why use a click event for the button?
options: So the check runs exactly when the player clicks
quiz.explain: A click event runs your code at the moment the user clicks, which is when you want to check the guess.

project.title: Number Guessing Game in the Browser
project.brief: Build a guessing game on a web page: the computer picks a secret number from 1 to 20, the player types guesses, and the page gives hints until the player wins.
checks: The page has an input box, a button and a message area.
The computer picks a random number from 1 to 20.
The page says 'too high' or 'too low' after each wrong guess.
The game counts the number of tries.
The game shows a win message when the guess is right.
The game handles a guess that is not a number without breaking.

days.title: Arrays
days.goal: Store many items in an array and read, add and remove them.

video.title: JavaScript Arrays: Index, push, pop, slice, splice (Beginners #8)

steps: Make an array of five foods and log the whole array.
Log the first item with foods[0] and the last with foods[foods.length - 1].
Add an item with push() and remove the last with pop(), then log the array.
Log foods.length to count the items.
days.task: Make a shopping list array, add two items, remove one, and log the final list.
days.challenge: Make an array of numbers and log the biggest with Math.max(...numbers).

quiz.q: What position does the first item in an array have?
quiz.explain: Arrays start counting at 0. The first item is at index 0.

options: It adds an item to the end of an array
quiz.explain: push() adds one or more items to the end of an array.

options: How many items are in the array
quiz.explain: length is the count of items in the array.

days.title: Loops: for and while
days.goal: Repeat work with for and while loops.

video.title: JavaScript Fetch API using Async/Await

steps: Use a for loop to log the numbers 1 to 10.
Loop through an array of names and log each one.
Use a while loop that counts from 1 to 5.
Add up all the numbers in an array with a loop and log the total.
days.task: Print the 7 times table from 7 x 1 to 7 x 12 using a for loop.
days.challenge: Loop through a list of words and log only the ones longer than 4 letters.

quiz.q: What does for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) do?
options: It runs 5 times with i going 0 to 4
quiz.explain: It starts i at 0, runs while i is less than 5, and adds 1 each round: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.

quiz.q: When does a while loop stop?
quiz.explain: A while loop repeats while its condition is true and stops when it becomes false.

quiz.q: What does break do in a loop?
quiz.explain: break exits the loop straight away.

days.title: Functions
days.goal: Write your own functions to reuse code.

video.title: How to FETCH data from an API using JavaScript

steps: Write a function greet(name) that logs a greeting, then call it.
Write a function add(a, b) that returns the sum, and log add(3, 4).
Write an arrow function double = n => n * 2 and log double(5).
Write a function that takes an array of numbers and returns the average.
days.task: Write three functions: celsiusToFahrenheit, fahrenheitToCelsius, and a small test that logs both conversions.
days.challenge: Write a function that takes a sentence and returns how many words it has.

quiz.q: What does return do in a function?
options: It sends a value back to the caller
quiz.explain: return hands a value back to the code that called the function.
Arrow functions use => and are a shorter way to write functions, like n => n * 2.

options: To reuse code, avoid repeating yourself and keep programs tidy
quiz.explain: Functions let you write logic once and call it many times.

days.title: Objects
days.goal: Store data as key-value pairs in objects.

video.title: JavaScript Full Course for Beginners | Complete All-in-One Tutorial | 8 Hours

steps: Make an object for a person with name, age and city keys, then log it.
Log one value with person.name and one with person['age'].
Add a new key and change an existing value.
Add a method to the object, like greet() that logs a greeting.
days.task: Build a small product object with name, price and stock, plus a method that logs a summary.
days.challenge: Make an array of three person objects and log each person's name in a loop.

quiz.q: What is an object in JavaScript?
quiz.explain: An object stores named values, like {name: 'Ada', age: 25}, and you read them by key.

quiz.q: How do you read the name from person?
quiz.explain: Dot notation, person.name, reads the value stored under the key 'name'.

options: A function stored inside an object
quiz.explain: A method is a function that lives on an object and usually works with that object's data.

days.title: Array Methods: map, filter, find
days.goal: Transform and search arrays with map, filter and find.

video.title: Full JavaScript Course for Beginners

steps: Use map() to double every number in an array.
Use filter() to keep only the numbers bigger than 10.
Use find() to get the first item that matches a condition.
Use forEach() to log every item in an array.
days.task: Given an array of prices, use map() to add 10% tax to each and log the new prices.
days.challenge: Filter a list of names to only the ones that start with the letter A.

options: A new array with the same length, each item changed by your function
quiz.explain: map() runs your function on every item and returns a new array of the results.

options: A new array with only the items that pass your test
quiz.explain: filter() keeps only the items where your test returns true, and returns them as a new array.

options: The first item that passes the test, or undefined
quiz.explain: find() returns the first matching item, or undefined if nothing matches.

days.title: The DOM: Selecting Elements
days.goal: Find and read parts of a web page with JavaScript.

video.title: JavaScript Tutorial for Beginners - Full Course in 12 Hours (2022)

steps: Use document.getElementById('title') to grab a heading.
Use document.querySelector('.card') to grab the first element with a class.
Use querySelectorAll('li') to grab all list items and log how many there are.
Read an element's textContent and log it.
days.task: Build a page with three paragraphs and log each one's text to the console.
days.challenge: Select all the buttons on a page and log how many there are.

options: A tree-like model of the page that JavaScript can read and change
quiz.explain: The DOM is the browser's model of the page. JavaScript uses it to find and change elements.
It returns the single element whose id is 'title'.

quiz.q: What is the difference between querySelector and querySelectorAll?
options: querySelector returns the first match, querySelectorAll returns all matches
quiz.explain: querySelector gives the first match. querySelectorAll gives a list of every match.

days.title: Project 2: To-Do List Web App
days.goal: Build a to-do list that runs in the browser.

video.title: JavaScript Full Course For Beginners With JavaScript Projects

steps: Make a page with an input, an Add button and an empty list.
When Add is clicked, create a new <li> with the task text and add it to the list.
Add a Delete button to each task that removes it when clicked.
Clear the input box after each task is added.
days.task: Finish the to-do app and add five real tasks to it.
days.challenge: Add a checkbox to each task that crosses the text out when ticked.

quiz.q: How do you create a new element in JavaScript?
quiz.explain: createElement() makes a new element you can fill with text and add to the page.

quiz.q: How do you add an element to the page?
quiz.explain: appendChild() adds a new element as the last child of a parent element.

quiz.q: Why clear the input after adding a task?
options: So the user can type the next task without deleting the old text
quiz.explain: Clearing the input keeps the app smooth: the user types the next task straight away.

project.title: To-Do List Web App
project.brief: Build a to-do list that runs in the browser: add tasks, show them in a list, and delete them. Tasks must survive a page refresh using local storage.
checks: The page has an input, an Add button and a list.
Clicking Add creates a new task in the list.
Each task has a Delete button that removes it.
Tasks are saved to localStorage and loaded on refresh.
The input clears after each task is added.
Empty tasks cannot be added.

days.title: The DOM: Changing Text and Styles
days.goal: Change what a page shows and how it looks with JavaScript.

video.title: JavaScript Tutorial For Beginners

steps: Change a heading's text with element.textContent = 'New title'.
Change a paragraph's colour with element.style.color = 'red'.
Add a class to an element with classList.add('highlight').
Change an image's source with img.src = 'new.jpg'.
days.task: Build a page with a button that changes the page background colour each time it is clicked.
days.challenge: Make a button that hides and shows a paragraph each time it is clicked.

options: It gets or sets the text inside an element
quiz.explain: textContent reads or replaces the text inside an element.

options: It adds the class 'dark' to the element
quiz.explain: classList.add() puts a CSS class on the element so your stylesheet can style it.

quiz.q: Why use classes instead of setting style directly?
options: Classes keep styling in CSS, so design stays in one place
quiz.explain: Using classes keeps your styles in CSS where they belong, and lets you toggle designs easily.

days.title: Events: Clicks
days.goal: React when users click things on your page.

video.title: JavaScript Full Course for Beginners (2026): Build a Real Page

steps: Add a click event to a button with addEventListener('click', ...).
Make the button log 'Clicked!' each time it is pressed.
Make a counter button that adds 1 to a number on the page each click.
Add a second button that resets the counter to 0.
days.task: Build a like button that shows how many likes it has and increases by 1 each click.
days.challenge: Make three buttons that each change the page background to a different colour.

options: Code that waits for something to happen, like a click, then runs
quiz.explain: An event listener waits for an event on an element and runs your function when it happens.

options: It runs myFunction every time the element is clicked
quiz.explain: It registers myFunction to run whenever a click happens on that element.

options: An object with details about what happened, like which key was pressed
quiz.explain: The event object carries details about the event, such as the target element or the key pressed.

days.title: Events: Forms and Input
days.goal: Read what users type and handle form submissions properly.

video.title: Code Companion #9: DOM Manipulation

steps: Listen for the 'input' event on a text box and show what the user types live.
Listen for the 'submit' event on a form and stop the page reloading with preventDefault().
Read the form values and log them when the form is submitted.
Show a thank-you message on the page after submit.
days.task: Build a sign-up form that checks the name is not empty before showing a welcome message.
days.challenge: Make a live character counter that shows how many characters are left as you type.

quiz.q: Why call preventDefault() on a form submit?
options: To stop the browser reloading the page so JavaScript can handle the data
quiz.explain: By default a form submit reloads the page. preventDefault() stops that so your code can handle it.

quiz.q: Which event fires every time the user types in a box?
quiz.explain: The input event fires on every keystroke, which is perfect for live feedback.

quiz.q: How do you read a form field's value?
quiz.explain: Form fields store what the user typed in their .value property.

days.title: Timers: setTimeout and setInterval
days.goal: Run code after a delay or on a repeating schedule.

video.title: Asynchronous JavaScript 1 of 3: setTimeout, setInterval, clearInterval

steps: Use setTimeout() to log a message after 3 seconds.
Use setInterval() to log a number every second.
Store the interval id and stop it with clearInterval() after 5 seconds.
Build a countdown that shows 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, then 'Go!'.
days.task: Build a simple clock that shows the current time and updates every second.
days.challenge: Make a button that shows a message, then hides it again after 2 seconds.

options: It runs code once after a delay
quiz.explain: setTimeout() waits the delay you give, then runs your function once.

options: It runs code again and again on a schedule
quiz.explain: setInterval() repeats your function every few milliseconds until you stop it.

quiz.q: How do you stop an interval?
options: Call clearInterval() with the id that setInterval() returned
quiz.explain: setInterval() returns an id. Pass that id to clearInterval() to stop it.

days.title: JSON
days.goal: Understand JSON and turn it into JavaScript objects and back.

video.title: JavaScript Fetch API using Async/Await

steps: Use JSON.parse() to turn a JSON string into an object.
Use JSON.stringify() to turn an object into a JSON string.
Log the type of the parsed result to confirm it is an object.
Access a nested value like data.user.name.
days.task: Take a JSON string of a product and log its name and price.
days.challenge: Turn an array of tasks into a JSON string and log it.

options: A text format for data, using keys and values like JavaScript objects
quiz.explain: JSON is plain text shaped like objects and arrays, used to send data between programs.

options: It turns a JSON string into a real JavaScript value
It saves JSON to a file
quiz.explain: JSON.parse() reads JSON text and gives you back an object or array you can use.

options: It turns a JavaScript value into a JSON text string
quiz.explain: stringify() turns an object or array into a JSON string you can send or store.

days.title: Fetch API Basics
days.goal: Ask a server for data with fetch() and read the reply.

video.title: How to FETCH data from an API using JavaScript

steps: Use fetch() to request a public JSON API and log the response.
Use .then() to turn the reply into JSON with response.json().
Log one value from the data, like the title of a post.
Add .catch() to log a friendly message if the request fails.
days.task: Fetch a random joke from a public API and show it on your page.
days.challenge: Fetch a list of users and log only their names.

options: A promise that will hold the response
quiz.explain: fetch() returns a promise. The data arrives later, so you handle it with .then() or await.

options: An object that represents a value that is not ready yet
quiz.explain: A promise is a placeholder for a future value. It can be pending, fulfilled or rejected.

options: It runs when the promise fails, so you can handle the error
quiz.explain: .catch() runs if the request fails, letting you show a friendly message instead of crashing.

days.title: Project 3: Weather App
days.goal: Build a weather app that fetches real data from a free API.

video.title: JavaScript Full Course for Beginners | Complete All-in-One Tutorial | 8 Hours

steps: Make a page with a city input, a button and a result area.
Use fetch() to ask a free weather API for the city.
Show the temperature, weather description and city name on the page.
Show 'City not found' when the API cannot find the city.
days.task: Finish the weather app and test it with three different cities.
days.challenge: Add the wind speed and a small icon or emoji for the weather type.

quiz.q: Why check response.ok before reading the data?
options: Because a failed request may not contain the data you expect
quiz.explain: response.ok tells you the request worked. If not, the body may be an error message.

options: It pauses the function until the promise finishes, then gives the value
quiz.explain: await pauses an async function until the promise settles, so you can write code that reads top to bottom.

quiz.q: Why use a free public API for this project?
options: Because it is the only option
Because it gives real data without needing your own server or key
Because it is faster than local data
quiz.explain: Public APIs give you real live data to practise with, with no server to build.

project.title: Weather App with a Real API
project.brief: Build a weather app: the user types a city, the app fetches real weather data from a free public API, and shows the temperature and description on the page.
checks: The page has a city input, a button and a result area.
The app fetches data from a free weather API.
The temperature and weather description show on the page.
The app shows 'City not found' for a bad city name.
The app shows a friendly message when the network fails.
The code uses async/await or .then() to handle the fetch.

days.title: Async and Await
days.goal: Write clean async code with async functions and await.

video.title: Full JavaScript Course for Beginners

steps: Mark a function with async so it can use await.
Use await fetch() and await response.json() to get data step by step.
Wrap the code in try/catch to handle a failed request.
Call the async function and log the result.
days.task: Rewrite your joke fetcher using async/await instead of .then().
days.challenge: Fetch two APIs one after the other and log both results.

quiz.q: What does async do to a function?
options: It lets the function use await and makes it return a promise
quiz.explain: An async function can use await inside it, and it always returns a promise.

quiz.q: What does try/catch do with async code?
options: It catches errors from failed awaits so you can handle them
quiz.explain: try/catch around await catches a rejected promise, like a failed request, so you can show a message.

quiz.q: Why is async/await easier to read than .then() chains?
options: It reads top to bottom like normal code instead of nested callbacks
quiz.explain: await lets you write async steps in a straight line, which is easier to follow than chains of .then().

days.title: Error Handling
days.goal: Handle errors kindly so your app never breaks in front of the user.

video.title: JavaScript Tutorial for Beginners - Full Course in 12 Hours (2022)

steps: Wrap risky code in try/catch and log a friendly message in the catch.
Throw your own error with throw new Error('Bad input') when input is wrong.
Use a finally block to run clean-up code no matter what.
Test your code with bad input and confirm it shows a message, not a crash.
days.task: Make your weather app show a clear message when the network is off.
days.challenge: Write a function that throws an error for a negative age and catches it.

options: It tries code and runs a backup plan if an error happens
quiz.explain: try runs code that might fail. If it fails, catch runs instead of crashing the page.

options: It creates an error on purpose so calling code can handle it
quiz.explain: throw creates an error you can catch, which is handy for invalid input.

options: It runs only when there is no error
It runs whether or not an error happened
quiz.explain: finally runs at the end no matter what, which is handy for clean-up.

days.title: Local Storage
days.goal: Save data in the browser so it survives a page refresh.

video.title: JavaScript Full Course For Beginners With JavaScript Projects

steps: Use localStorage.setItem('name', 'Ada') to save a value.
Use localStorage.getItem('name') to read it back after a refresh.
Save an array by turning it into JSON with JSON.stringify() first.
Read it back with JSON.parse() and log the array.
days.task: Make your to-do app save its tasks to local storage so they survive a refresh.
days.challenge: Save a dark mode setting and apply it when the page loads.

options: A small storage space in the browser that keeps data after refresh
quiz.explain: localStorage lets you save key-value pairs in the browser. They stay there until you delete them.
localStorage only stores strings, so you turn objects into JSON text first.

quiz.q: How do you save an array in localStorage?
options: Turn it into a JSON string with JSON.stringify() first
quiz.explain: Because localStorage only stores strings, you stringify the array, then parse it back when reading.

days.title: Build a Calculator
days.goal: Put functions, events and the DOM together in a calculator app.

video.title: JavaScript Tutorial For Beginners

steps: Make a page with buttons for digits and operations and a display area.
When a digit button is clicked, add the digit to the display.
When = is clicked, work out the answer with a function and show it.
Add a Clear button that empties the display.
days.task: Finish the calculator and test add, subtract, multiply and divide.
days.challenge: Add a backspace button that deletes the last digit.

quiz.q: How should the calculator store the current number?
options: In a variable that updates as buttons are clicked
quiz.explain: Keep the current value in a variable, show it in the display, and update both on each click.

quiz.q: Why use one function per operation?
options: So each operation is easy to test and fix
quiz.explain: One function per operation keeps the code tidy and each piece easy to check.

quiz.q: What should dividing by zero show?
options: A friendly message like 'Cannot divide by zero'
quiz.explain: A good app catches the problem and explains it instead of breaking.

days.title: Build a Memory Game
days.goal: Build a card matching game with JavaScript and the DOM.

video.title: JavaScript Full Course for Beginners (2026): Build a Real Page

steps: Make 8 cards (4 pairs) with JavaScript and shuffle them.
When a card is clicked, flip it to show its symbol.
When two cards are flipped, check if they match.
If they match, keep them face up. If not, flip them back after a short delay.
days.task: Finish the memory game and play it until you match all pairs.
days.challenge: Add a move counter and a win message that shows how many moves it took.

quiz.q: How do you shuffle an array of cards?
options: Use a shuffle: loop through and swap each item with a random one
quiz.explain: A shuffle swaps each item with a random other item, which mixes the order.

quiz.q: Why use setTimeout when two cards do not match?
options: To give the player a moment to see both cards before they flip back
quiz.explain: A short delay lets the player see the two cards before they turn face down again.

quiz.q: How do you know the game is won?
quiz.explain: The game is won when every pair has been found and stays face up.

days.title: Build a Countdown Timer
days.goal: Build a countdown timer with setInterval and the DOM.

video.title: Code Companion #9: DOM Manipulation

steps: Make a page with a minutes input and a Start button.
When Start is clicked, begin a setInterval that ticks every second.
Show the remaining time as minutes and seconds on the page.
When the time reaches zero, stop the interval and show 'Time is up!'.
days.task: Finish the countdown timer and test it with 1 minute.
days.challenge: Add a Pause button that stops the timer and a Resume button that starts it again.

quiz.q: How do you turn total seconds into minutes and seconds?
options: Minutes = total seconds divided by 60 (rounded down), seconds = the remainder
quiz.explain: Minutes are total seconds // 60 and the leftover seconds are total seconds % 60.

options: So you can stop the timer later with clearInterval(id)
quiz.explain: You need the id to stop that exact interval with clearInterval().

quiz.q: What happens if you start the timer twice without stopping it?
options: Two intervals run and the countdown goes twice as fast
quiz.explain: Starting twice creates two intervals, so the count drops twice per second. Always stop the old one first.

steps: Open a page with a bug, press F12 and read the error in the Console.

quiz.q: What does the Console tab show you?
options: Errors, warnings and your console.log() messages
quiz.explain: The Console shows JavaScript errors and anything you log, which is your first stop when something breaks.

quiz.q: Why read the error message first?
options: Because it usually names the error type and the exact line that failed
quiz.explain: Error messages point at the file and line, which saves you from guessing.

quiz.q: What makes a good project demo?
options: A clear explanation of the problem, the solution and a live run

options: The problem, the features, the tools used and how you will show it

capstone.title: Build and Share a Useful Web App
capstone.brief: Build a complete web app that solves a real problem for real people: a budget tracker, a study planner, a small shop page or a habit tracker. It must have a clean page, working buttons, data saved in local storage, and at least one fetch from a public API. Share it on GitHub Pages with a README and a short demo.
checks: The app solves one real problem and you can explain the problem in one sentence.
It has a clean HTML page and CSS styling.
Buttons and inputs work with JavaScript and the DOM.
Data is saved in localStorage so it survives a refresh.
It fetches data from at least one public API.
It is live on GitHub Pages with a README that explains how to use it.
You can show a live demo and explain how it works in simple words.
deliverables: A working web app (HTML, CSS and JavaScript files).
A live GitHub Pages link to the app.
A README.md explaining the problem, the features and how to use it.
A short demo video or screenshots showing the app running.
A one-page write-up of what you learned in 30 days.
